title: Woman dies in police cell shortly after arrest
subtitle: Deceased had been arrested for possession of drugs for the purpose of trafficking
article: The civilian agency that investigates deaths and serious injuries involving police officers was in South Frontenac yesterday trying to figure out what role, if any, five Frontenac OPP officers may have played in the sudden death of a woman in police custody early yesterday morning.

The Toronto-based Special Investigations Unit dispatched five investigators, including two forensic specialists, to Frontenac OPP headquarters in the village of Hartington yesterday, said SIU spokeswoman Rose Bliss.

"We're really looking at the time \[period from\] when she was arrested until the time she died ... but we're going to focus on what exactly happened in the police cell and what led to her medical distress," Bliss said yesterday.

The deceased woman was taken into police custody with a 49-year- old man around 2:30 a.m., after provincial police searched a home for drugs. The man and woman were arrested for possession for the purpose of trafficking.
About 20 minutes after they were logged into cells at the Frontenac OPP detachment, the woman, who had been arrested without incident, went into medical distress.
According to a release from the OPP, officers immediately called emergency services and the woman was rushed by ambulance to Kingston General Hospital where she was pronounced dead.
Bliss would not elaborate on the definition of medical distress in this case.
She also would not release the woman's name yesterday because her family had not yet been notified of her death.
OPP spokeswoman Sgt. Kristine Cholette wouldn't release the man's name yesterday because he hadn't been formally charged in court.
Cholette also wouldn't reveal the address where the drug search had been conducted, except that it took place on Harrowsmith Road.

Bliss said the SIU investigators planned to spend yesterday interviewing police officers and examining the cell where the deceased woman was kept and all relevant records that might point to the extent of police involvement in her death.
A post-mortem investigation was held in Kingston yesterday to determine the cause of death.
But, until it and a full investigation of the events leading up to the woman's death are complete, Bliss said she can't release more details about the case.
"We won't be able to release any results from the post-mortem examination because that's pertinent to what we're investigating - the cause of her death, the factors surrounding her death," she said.
SIU investigators are familiar with the Kingston area. They have been to this region several times in the past to investigate deaths or accidents involving civilians and police officers.
They were last in this area in November when they were investigating the shooting death of a young Elgin man.
Jason Steacy, 20, was fatally wounded during a confrontation with police at his trailer home on Wilson Street in Elgin.

The shooting occurred after provincial police were called to deal with a man who was reportedly trying to get into another home in the trailer park. There, police found Elgin resident Todd Burtch suffering from stab wounds to the neck.
Soon afterward, police confronted Steacy in his trailer.
